ἐτίσατο: τίνω (mid. τίνυμαι) — pay, requite; mid. exact vengeance, take vengeance on; aor. 3 sg. mid.: ’took vengeance (on)’
ἐϋκτιμένην: ἐΰκτίμενος — well-built, well-founded; fem. acc. sg., epic ἐϋ- (= εὖ); said of a town
ἐών: εἰμί — be; pres. part. masc. nom. sg., epic ἐών (= Attic ὤν): ’being’
ἑλλάδα: Ἑλλάς — Hellas, a district beside Phthia in Achilles’ realm; fem. acc. sg.
ἔβαλεν: βάλλω — throw, hurl, strike; aor. 3 sg., ν-movable: ’threw’ (κὰδ … ἔβαλεν = κατέβαλεν ’laid low’)
ἔθεντο: τίθημι — put, set; mid. make for oneself; aor. 3 pl. mid.: ’made for themselves’ (οἰκία ἔθεντο ’made their homes’)
ἔκτανε: κτείνω — kill, slay; aor. 3 sg., strong aorist ἔκτανον: ’killed’
ἔλαιον: ἔλαιον — olive oil; neut. nom. sg., after ἠΰτε: ’like oil’
ἔλαυνε: ἐλαύνω — drive; impf. 3 sg., without the lengthened augment (= Attic ἤλαυνε): ’drove’
ἔννεπε: ἐννέπω — tell of, relate, speak; pres. imper. 2 sg.
ἔτεκεν: τίκτω — bear, beget; aor. 3 sg., augmented, ν-movable: ’bore’
ἔχεν: ἔχω — have, hold; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= εἶχεν): ’held’
ἕλκεϊ: ἕλκος — wound, sore; neut. dat. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic ἕλκει)
ἕλληνες: Ἕλληνες — the Hellenes, a people of Achilles’ realm; masc. nom. pl.
ἕστασαν: ἵστημι — stand; plpf. 3 pl., intransitive (= Attic εἱστήκεσαν): ’stood, were standing’ (reduplicated ἑ-στα-σαν)
ἠλώνην: Ἠλώνη — Elone, a town of Perrhaebia in Thessaly; fem. acc. sg.
ἠϋκόμοιο: ἠΰκομος (= ἐΰκομος) — fair-haired; adj. of two endings, fem. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου), agreeing with Βρισηΐδος
ἡγήσαιτο: ἡγέομαι — lead the way, guide (+ dat.); aor. opt. 3 sg., in a relative clause of characteristic after a negative: ’who might lead’
ἡγείσθην: ἡγέομαι — lead, go before (+ gen.); impf. 3 dual: ’the two led’
ἡγεμόνος: ἡγεμών — guide, leader; masc. gen. sg., after a verb of lacking (+ gen.)
ἡμιτελής: ἡμιτελής — half-finished, half-complete; adj. of two endings, masc. nom. sg., agreeing with δόμος
ἡρακλεΐδαο: Ἡρακλεΐδης — son of Heracles (patronymic); masc. gen. sg., epic -αο (= Attic -ου), in apposition to Θεσσαλοῦ
ἦρχεν: ἄρχω — begin, rule, lead; impf. 3 sg., ν-movable, + gen.: ’was leading’
ἰαωλκόν: Ἰαωλκός — Iolcus, a town of Thessaly; fem. acc. sg. (Ἰαωλκόν)
ἰδὲ: ἰδέ — and; epic conj. (= Attic καί)
ἰητῆρ: ἰητήρ — healer, physician; masc. nom. dual, elided (ἰητῆρ’ = ἰητῆρε)
ἰθώμην: Ἰθώμη — Ithome, a town of Thessaly; fem. acc. sg.
ἰφίκλου: Ἴφικλος — Iphiclus, father of Podarces; masc. gen. sg.
ἱέντες: ἵημι — throw, hurl, let fly; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’throwing’
ἱμερτὸν: ἱμερτός — lovely, desirable; masc. acc. sg., agreeing with Τιταρησσόν
ἱπποδάμεια: Ἱπποδάμεια — Hippodameia, wife of Peirithous; fem. nom. sg.
ἴτωνά: Ἴτων — Iton, a town; acc. sg. (Ἴτωνα), accented before the enclitic τε
ὀλιζῶνα: Ὀλιζών — Olizon, a town among Philoctetes’ places; fem. acc. sg. (Ὀλιζῶνα)
ὀλοοσσόνα: Ὀλοοσσών — Oloosson, a town of Thessaly; fem. acc. sg. (Ὀλοοσσόνα), in apposition to πόλιν
ὀλοόφρονος: ὀλοόφρων — baleful-minded (sense of the epithet debated); adj. of two endings, masc. gen. sg., agreeing with ὕδρου
ὀρμένιον: Ὀρμένιον — Ormenium, a town of Thessaly; acc. sg.
ὀϊλῆϊ: Ὀϊλεύς — Oileus, father of the lesser Ajax; masc. dat. sg., epic -ῆϊ (= Attic -εῖ)
ὁπλότερος: ὁπλότερος — younger; comparative adj. (superl. ὁπλότατος); masc. nom. sg.
ὄρθην: Ὄρθη — Orthe, a town of Thessaly; fem. acc. sg.
ὄτριχας: ὄθριξ (lemma uncertain) — alike in hair, of one coat (traditional sense; the word is not secure); adj., acc. pl. ὄτριχας
ὅθι: ὅθι — where; epic relative adverb (= Attic οὗ)
ὑπέρειαν: Ὑπέρεια — Hypereia, a spring of Thessaly; fem. acc. sg., in apposition to κρήνην
ὑπερθύμοιο: ὑπέρθυμος — high-spirited (ὑπέρ + θυμός); masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
ὕδατός: ὕδωρ — water; neut. gen. sg., accented before an enclitic
ῥήνη: Ῥήνη — Rhene, mother of Medon; fem. nom. sg.

__broaden__.αὐτῶν: αὐτός — self; gen. pl. as the plain personal pronoun after a preposition: ’them’ (ἐπ’ αὐτῶν ’on them’) · also gen. pl. dependent on a noun, ’of them’ (ἄνυσις … αὐτῶν ’accomplishment of them’) · also intensive, gen. pl. agreeing with a noun: ’of the men themselves’ (ποδῶν αὐτῶν τε καὶ ἵππων ’of the very men’s feet and of the horses’) · also gen. pl. standing alone for the men, as against their horses: ’of the men themselves’ (αὐτῶν ἠδ’ ἵππων ’of the men and of the horses’)
__broaden__.εἰνοσίφυλλον: εἰνοσίφυλλος — leaf-shaking, with quivering foliage; adj. of two endings, acc. sg., agreeing with Νήριτον · also neut. acc. sg., agreeing with Πήλιον
__broaden__.κλυτὸς: κλυτός — famous, renowned; adj., masc. nom. sg. · also the masc. form used with a fem. name, nom. sg., agreeing with Ἱπποδάμεια
__broaden__.παρ: παρά (elided παρ’) — beside, by; + acc.: ’along, beside’ (παρ’ αὐτὸν) · also + gen., ’from beside’ (παρ’ Εὐρύτου ’from Eurytus’) · also prep. + dat.: ’beside’ (παρ’ ἅρμασιν ’beside the chariots’)
__broaden__.περὶ: περί — around; + gen.: ’beyond, above’, or adv. ’exceedingly’ · also preverb in tmesis ’all round’ · also adv. in tmesis with εἰμί: ’surpass’ (περὶ … ἐστέ) · also + dat. of place: ’around’ (περὶ δουρί ’around the spear’) · also with ἀμφί, both before an accusative, ’round about’ (ἀμφὶ περὶ κρήνην ’round about a spring’) · also prep. + acc. of place: ’around’ (περὶ Δωδώνην ’around Dodona’)
__broaden__.ποδάρκης: ποδάρκης — swift-footed; masc. nom. sg., epithet of Achilles · also Ποδάρκης — Podarces, son of Iphiclus, leader of the men of Phylace; masc. nom. sg., proper name
__broaden__.πρότερος: πρότερος — before, first, earlier; masc. nom. sg., predicative: ’first (to)’ · also predicate, ’earlier-born, elder’ (ὁ δ’ ἅμα πρότερος ’and he was the elder’)
__broaden__.πτελεὸν: Πτελεός — Pteleum, a town of Messenia; acc. sg. · also Πτελεός — Pteleum, a town of Thessaly; acc. sg., with λεχεποίην
__broaden__.τίς: τίς, τί — who? what?; interrog. pron., masc./fem. nom. sg. · also indefinite τις after ὅς, written τίς: ’anyone, someone’ (ὅς τίς σφιν … ἡγήσαιτο ’anyone to lead them’)
__broaden__.τὸ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. sg., ’this, that’ · also relative, neut. nom. sg.: ’which’ (σκῆπτρον, τὸ … οὔ ποτε φύλλα φύσει) · also neut. acc. sg. with a noun, article-like: ’the, that’ (τὸ Πελασγικὸν Ἄργος ’the Pelasgian Argos’)
__broaden__.τῆς: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun); fem. gen. sg. · also fem. gen. sg. with the force of a relative: ’of which’ · also fem. gen. sg. ’for her’, gen. of cause after ἀχέων (τῆς … ἀχέων ’grieving for her’)
__broaden__.ἄργος: Ἄργος — Argos, the Argive land (Greece); neut. nom./acc. sg. · also the Pelasgian Argos, a district of northern Greece; neut. acc. sg.
__broaden__.ἐΐσας: ἐΐσος (ἔΐσος) — equal, even, balanced (of ships, sense uncertain); fem. acc. pl., epic · also of mares, ’balanced, level’ (ἐπὶ νῶτον ἐΐσας ’balanced along the back’)
__broaden__.ἔνθα: ἔνθα — there, then; adverb of place or time · also relative, ’where’ (ἔνθα πάρος κοιμᾶθ’ ’where he used to sleep’) · also ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα ’hither and thither, this way and that’
__broaden__.ἔργα: ἔργον — deed, work; neut. nom./acc. pl. · also ’tilled land, farmland’ (ἔργα νέμοντο ’inhabited the farmlands’)
__broaden__.ὄφρ: ὄφρα (elided ὄφρ’) — so that, in order that; epic; + subj. · also temporal, ’as long as, while’ + indic. (ὄφρ’ Ἀχιλεὺς μήνιεν ’while Achilles was angry’)
__broaden__.ὑπ: ὑπό (elided ὑπ’) — under, beneath; + gen.: ’from under’ (ὑπ’ ἀνθερεῶνος) · also + gen. of the agent or cause, ’under’ (ἀϋσάντων ὑπ’ Ἀχαιῶν ’as the Achaeans shouted’) · also prep. + dat. with τίκτω, of the father: ’to’ (ὑπ’ Ἀδμήτῳ τέκε ’bore to Admetus’)
__broaden__.ὑπὸ: ὑπό — under, beneath; adv. and preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ὑπὸ … τάνυσσαν ’stretched under’) · also prep. + acc. of motion: ’to, under’ (ὑπὸ Ἴλιον ἦλθον ’came to Ilios’) · also prep. + dat., ’under, beneath’ (ὑπὸ πλατανίστῳ ’beneath a plane-tree’) · also prep. + dat. with τίκτω, of the father: ’to’ (ὑπὸ Πειριθόῳ τέκετο ’bore to Peirithous’)
__broaden__.ἐπὶ: ἐπί — on, upon, to, against; + dat./acc./gen.; also a preverb in tmesis (ἐπὶ … ἔτελλε = ἐπέτελλε) · also + dat., ’in aid of, on behalf of’ (ἐπὶ Τρώεσσιν ἀρῆξαι ’to help the Trojans’) · also + acc. of duration, ’for’ (ἐπὶ χρόνον ’for a time’) · also + acc. of extent, ’over, along’ (ἐπὶ νῶτον ’along the back’)
